features.title: Preview iframe boundary
features.summary: The boundary between the Workbench and the Preview iframe: what the iframe owns, how the Workbench observes and controls it, and where review chrome is drawn.

rules.statement: For normal control and inspection the Workbench never reads or changes the Preview iframe's DOM, Widget Runtime or Blueprint objects, even when both share an origin; it uses only the Preview protocol or a dedicated channel.

The Preview iframe owns Widget hit testing, Widget identity resolution and Widget geometry, and gives the Workbench only canonical UIUX identities with structural or geometry data, never raw DOM, Runtime or Blueprint objects.
The Workbench draws all review chrome, including hover and selection highlights, comment pins, composers and threads, outside the iframe; the Preview document never renders review chrome.
The Preview protocol is owned by UIUX: reused devtools primitives stay behind a UIUX bridge, and UIUX never depends on Widget Lab modules or adopts the widget-devtools wire protocol as its own.

features.title: Preview session and runtime lifecycle
features.summary: The Preview session and runtime generation lifecycle: session and generation identity and history, reload, restart and reconnect boundaries, and automatic and explicit recovery of a failed generation.

rules.statement: A Preview session spans iframe reloads, runtime restarts, transport reconnects, View and Variant navigation and generation changes; only a new Preview instance starts a new session, together with an empty history of retired generations.
The Workbench never activates a Preview session whose ID matches one retired earlier in the same Workbench process; it discards that ID and generates another before the session begins.
After a full Workbench restart, an open Workbench page starts a new Preview session, with a fresh generation and newly acquired geometry, before any geometry traffic resumes.
A runtime generation that becomes protocol-invalid ends only that generation, never the enclosing Preview session.
After a generation becomes protocol-invalid, the runtime may start one fresh generation automatically in the same Preview session, with its own declaration and acknowledgement.
If the automatic recovery generation also becomes protocol-invalid during its handshake, no further generation starts until the Workbench authorizes an explicit retry.
The automatic recovery allowance renews only when a fresh generation completes its handshake; creating a generation, declaring capabilities, reconnecting or waiting never renews it.
While recovery is exhausted and no retry is authorized, the Workbench never acknowledges a new generation or accepts its traffic, and retires its ID without ending the Preview session.
While Preview capability is unavailable, the Workbench sends and accepts no geometry traffic, keeps the structural Widget selection and shows the highlight as unavailable.
One explicit retry authorizes exactly one fresh-generation attempt; if that generation fails, Preview returns to capability-unavailable and the automatic allowance stays spent.
A retry authorization is spent when its fresh generation enters bootstrap, whatever the outcome of that generation's handshake.
A pending retry authorization lasts until it is spent, revoked or its Preview session ends; time, reconnects, reloads and navigation never expire it.
A retry trigger while an authorization is pending joins that authorization, so retry attempts never accumulate.
The Workbench may revoke a pending retry authorization before its generation enters bootstrap; revocation and admission are serialized, and whichever commits first wins.
A retry trigger while an authorized generation is still in its handshake creates no authorization and never replaces or cancels that generation.
Iframe reloads, runtime restarts, reconnects and View or Variant navigation never clear exhausted recovery or authorize a new generation.
A new Preview session starts with an unspent automatic recovery allowance, no unavailable state and no retry authorization.

After a generation change the Workbench hides every highlight of the old generation and draws it again only from a complete geometry set acquired under the new generation, never showing old contours meanwhile.

- {{R.preview.session.restart}}: Not built as of 6171f5d: when the page reconnects to a restarted server it re-reads the Workspace but keeps its Preview session, generation and geometry state (`app/composables/useConnectivity.ts#L63-L71`, `app/composables/usePreviewSession.ts#L109-L110`); tracked in issue #101 (https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/issues/101).

- {{R.preview.session.retry-one-attempt}}: Bug as of 6171f5d: the Retry action replaces the generation as a reload instead of spending an explicit retry authorization, so after a capability failure the session refuses the new generation as unauthorized and Preview keeps showing that it is connecting (`app/composables/usePreviewSession.ts#L592-L615`, `src/preview/protocol/session.ts#L78-L83`); tracked in issue #101 (https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/issues/101).

- {{R.preview.session.retry-revoke}}: Partly built as of 6171f5d: `PreviewProtocolSession` implements it (`src/preview/protocol/session.ts#L97-L105`, `#L175-L187`), but no Workbench action authorizes, spends or revokes a retry; tracked in issue #101 (https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/issues/101).

## Notes

- Added beyond the plan's Feature list: Discussion #1 comments 120-148 (session, generation and capability lifecycle) had no Feature home. Per the owner's Q1 ruling the wire-level detail will be Clauses of the Preview protocol Contract (message types and invariants only).
- The wire side of the lifecycle is owned by the Preview protocol Contract: identities by {{C.preview-protocol.session-id}} and {{C.preview-protocol.generation-id}}, retirement and reuse by {{C.preview-protocol.generation-reuse}}, the gates by {{C.preview-protocol.gates}} and {{C.preview-protocol.stale}}, the handshake by {{C.preview-protocol.handshake-gate}}, {{C.preview-protocol.declaration-pinning}} and {{C.preview-protocol.retransmission}}, and reload, restart and reconnect by {{C.preview-protocol.generation-boundaries}} and {{C.preview-protocol.generation-scope}}.
- The "Workbench process" of Discussion #1 c129 and c130 is the UIUX server process; retired session IDs are therefore process-local (c129). Failure categories, reason codes and the Retry Preview diagnostic are batch 6c (Preview failure diagnostics); what clears a refinement-failure latch (#1 c120) goes there with c118-c119.

contracts.title: Preview cross-iframe protocol
contracts.summary: The protocol between the Workbench and its Preview iframe: the wire channel and transport batches, the message envelope, field encoding and correlation context, Preview session and runtime generation identities and their gates, and the capability handshake.

clauses.statement: Protocol traffic travels by `postMessage` between the Workbench document and its Preview iframe as posts on the channel `uiux:preview:wire`: `{ channel, message }` with one envelope, or a batch `{ channel, messages }` with 1 to 256 envelopes and no other member. A receiver drops any other post on that channel whole.

A batch adds no identity, sequence, count or context of its own: the receiver passes each inner envelope, in order and independently, through the validation and gates of a single post, so an invalid envelope is rejected alone and a batch means exactly what the same envelopes sent as consecutive single posts mean.

Each side posts protocol traffic with its own origin as the target origin, never `*`, and accepts a post only when its origin equals its own and its source is the peer window: the current Preview iframe's window for the Workbench, the parent window for the Preview document.

Every protocol message is an envelope `{ type, context, payload }`: `type` is a non-empty, stable string from which the receiver selects the message schema, never inferred from the payload or a numeric code; `context` holds the shared correlation identities; `payload` holds all message-specific data, even when it is empty.

Required fields are always present, and an optional field that does not apply is omitted, never sent as `null` or another sentinel. A receiver ignores unknown fields of a known `type` while validating every known field; a field that a receiver must understand for correctness needs a capability or protocol-version gate.

The `context` key set is closed: `previewSessionId`, `runtimeGenerationId`, `viewId`, `variantId`, `runtimeContextVersion`, `navigationRequestId`, `widgetId` and `geometryRevision`, each present only when it applies to the message; `variantId` carries the Variant name and is omitted for the base state. Work-specific identities, such as contour-work sequences, snapshot versions, region IDs and interaction IDs, belong in `payload`.

`previewSessionId` is a non-empty opaque string that the Workbench generates fresh for each Preview session and gives the Preview document at bootstrap; the runtime only echoes it, and both sides compare it by equality, never by order.
`runtimeGenerationId` is a non-empty opaque string that the runtime generates fresh for each runtime generation; the Workbench never allocates it and compares it by equality, never by order.

A generation ID is retired for the rest of its Preview session once its generation ends, even if it was never acknowledged; a generation that reuses a retired ID is a non-recoverable protocol violation, and the Workbench rejects it and all its traffic.

Each side checks a received message's correlation outermost first: Preview session, runtime generation, then View, Variant and runtime context, navigation request and Widget, geometry revision, and last the work-specific identities such as contour-work sequence, base snapshot version and region IDs. The first mismatch makes the message stale.

A message that fails a correlation gate is stale and is discarded without effect: it is never staged for later, never adopted, never reactivates its generation and never by itself fails the current session or generation.

The handshake uses `capability.declare`, sent by the runtime with `payload` `{ protocolVersion, features }`, where `protocolVersion` is the protocol version the runtime implements, currently 1, and `capability.ack`, sent by the Workbench with `payload` `{}`. Their `context` carries only `previewSessionId` and `runtimeGenerationId`.

`features` is the generation's set of feature strings. Protocol version 1 defines `geometry`, `geometry.multi-target` and `widget.events`; adding an optional feature leaves `protocolVersion` unchanged, and the Workbench ignores a feature it does not know.

For each generation the runtime first sends `capability.declare`, echoing the session ID it was given. Until the runtime has received the matching `capability.ack` for that session and generation, neither side sends any other message type for that generation, and a receiver rejects any that arrive.

The first valid declaration of a generation pins its capability set before any acknowledgement. A later identical declaration in that generation is an idempotent duplicate that the Workbench answers with the same acknowledgement; a differing one makes the generation protocol-invalid, and the Workbench never acknowledges it.

A declaration without an acknowledgement keeps its generation, and the runtime may resend it unchanged; duplicate matching acknowledgements are idempotent and never acknowledged in turn. The protocol has no connection epoch, reconnect ID, handshake attempt ID, retry token or capability digest: the session and generation identify the handshake and its pinned capabilities.

A reloaded Preview document or a restarted runtime is a new generation with its own declaration and acknowledgement, and a retired generation is never revived. A pure transport reconnect keeps the session, the generation, its handshake state and in-flight requests, whose responses are accepted when they still pass the gates.

A new generation invalidates every geometry revision, region ID, contour-cache snapshot version and contour-work sequence of the previous generation; equal values in two generations never identify the same thing.

## Notes

- Owner ruling 2026-10-07 (batch 6a confirmation): the protocol decoders' validation diagnostic codes (`protocol.missing_context_identity`, `protocol.unknown_message_type`, `protocol.null_optional_field`, `protocol.identity_in_wrong_envelope`, `protocol.duplicate_capability_feature` and the like, `src/preview/protocol/schema.ts`) are non-normative; code at 6171f5d is authoritative. Only the failure reason registry of Discussion #2 (batch 6c) is a wire contract.
- Owner ruling Q1: the Preview protocol is imported as message types and invariants only. Payload field shapes beyond what an invariant needs stay authoritative in the protocol code types at 6171f5d (`src/preview/protocol/schema.ts`, `targeting.ts`, `widget-events.ts`, `transport.ts`), and algorithms and tolerance derivations stay in Discussions #1-#4.
- Import batch 6a creates this Contract with the transport, envelope, correlation, session, generation and capability-handshake Clauses. Batch 6b (navigation and geometry streams, targeting, Widget Events, pins) and batch 6c (contours, refinement, numeric conformance, failure diagnostics) extend it by naming it in full.
- Batching is optional for a sender: the runtime sends the envelopes of one task in one post, and the Workbench sends single envelopes (Discussion #2 c39). The per-frame reporting rate and the tracked-Widget cap are batch 6b.
- A `MessagePort` transport exists in code (`src/preview/protocol/message-port.ts`) but is not wired; once it is, port ownership replaces the source check of {{C.preview-protocol.origin}} (Discussion #2 c37 R15).
- Not imported: Discussion #1 c149-c150 and the migration comments Part 2 c1, Part 3 c1 and Part 4 c1 are discussion-map housekeeping; the Part 2 body's "Section rule" and each comment's "No implementation authorized" are process notes.
